item.title: Nick Siranni, Mike Vrabel don't address specifics regarding recent $250,000 fines
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: On Wednesday, a report emerged regarding significant fines imposed on three head coaches for their interactions with officials.
item.content:encoded:
On Wednesday, a report emerged regarding significant fines imposed on three head coaches for their interactions with officials. The news that the league dinged Patriots coach Mike Vrabel, Jets coach Aaron Glenn, and Eagles coach Nick Sirianni for $250,000 each lacked details about the behavior that caused it and the specific conditions that would keep the penalties, which reportedly are being held in abeyance, from being enforced.

Two of the coaches spoke to reporters on Thursday. Not much light was shed on the situation in either case.

"I won't get into my conversations with the league," Sirianni said when asked whether the fine was for a specific incident or something more general. "I try to keep everything player related, as far as my conversations with players, in-house. Not try, I do. Same with conversations with the league, same with conversations with the referees association. I'll just keep that at that."

He was then asked whether his approach to officials has changed in his tenure as a head coach.

"You are in constant growth," Sirianni said. "I truly believe that I've been in constant growth there in maturity in every phase. You're trying to get better as a coach on a daily basis. I'm always trying to get better as a human being, as a Christian, as a father, as a husband, as a son on a daily basis. I know that things don't happen overnight, and there are times where you 'relapse,' to say, and you have a moment that you want back. But I can truly see growth, and that happens because, again, my faith. That happens, again, because of the people I have around me. I want to continue to grow as a person and as a coach, but that doesn't mean we're perfect. We all fall and it's about how you get back up."

That still leaves us with nothing regarding what they said or did to trigger the fines. Which creates the impression that it was more of a warning shot by the league aimed at getting all coaches to go easier on the officials. The fact that Sirianni expressly referenced the NFL Referees Association lends credence to the idea that it's part of a broader effort to elevate the discourse.

Vrabel wasn't specifically asked about the fine after Thursday night's 30-24 loss to the Bears. In response to the last question of the press conference, he was asked about one of the calls made during the game.

"I'm not in very good favor with the officiating department," Vrabel said, "so I probably shouldn't say anything."

He walked off after that, leaving no opportunity for a follow-up.

Regardless, the issue cries out for more details. Why were they fined? What did they do? What is the standard of behavior for getting the fines rescinded?

Vrabel is next scheduled to talk to reporters on Monday. Perhaps at that point, we'll get some answers. Ditto for Glenn, who'll speak after Sunday's game against the Dolphins.

For now, the only lesson to other coaches is very broad: "Tread lightly." And maybe that was the entire goal of the imposition of the fines.

item.title: Report: Puka Nacua's calf injury not believed to be serious, but Week 7 status unclear
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Rams receiver Puka Nacua had to exit Thursday's practice with a calf injury, and now there's a bit of an update on him.
item.content:encoded:
Rams receiver Puka Nacua had to exit Thursday's practice with a calf injury, and now there's a bit of an update on him.

According to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, Nacua's calf injury is not believed to be serious. But it's still unclear whether or not he'll be able to play in Sunday's game against the Raiders, with Rapoport noting Nacua's status is "up in the air."

Los Angeles has been dealing with a wave of injuries this week, particularly on defense. But fellow receiver Davante Adams also went on injured reserve with a ruptured hamstring, thinning the team's depth at its skill positions.

Head coach Sean McVay is slated to speak with reporters on Friday before practice.

In four games this season, Nacua has caught 37 passes for 417 yards with one touchdown. He’s also rushed three times for 11 yards with 1 TD.

item.title: Kaden Elliss set to return for Saints, Cesar Ruiz listed as questionable
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Saints are set to get linebacker Kaden Elliss back in the lineup.
item.content:encoded:
The Saints are set to get linebacker Kaden Elliss back in the lineup.

Elliss has missed the last three games with a calf injury, but he has no injury designation for Sunday's game against the Steelers. Elliss had 24 tackles in the first three games of the season and his return will be welcomed by a team that ranks 31st in points allowed.

Right guard Cesar Ruiz returned to practice Friday after missing two days with a knee injury. He's listed as questionable to play in Paris this weekend.

An illness caused defensive lineman Nathan Shepherd to miss the team's final practice of the week. He's also listed as questionable for Week 7.

item.title: Steelers list Rico Dowdle, DeShon Elliott as questionable
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Steelers planned to have a walkthrough at Stade de France after arriving in Paris on Friday morning, but bad weather scrapped those plans and they'll hold their final practice ahead of Sunday's game against the Saints on Saturday.
item.content:encoded:
The Steelers planned to have a walkthrough at Stade de France after arriving in Paris on Friday morning, but bad weather scrapped those plans and they'll hold their final practice ahead of Sunday's game against the Saints on Saturday.

The team still had to issue injury designations for the game, however, and that report shows a pair of players have been listed as questionable. Running back Rico Dowdle (knee) and safety DeShon Elliott (knee) drew those designations.

Elliott has been designated for return from injured reserve, so the team will need to activate him by Saturday afternoon in order for him to play. They have open spots on the 53-man roster, so that move would not require any corresponding cut.

Linebacker T.J. Watt has no designation after being added to the injury report with a calf issue on Thursday. Watt was limited in that practice, but the team said he would have been a full participant on Friday and head coach Mike McCarthy said he does not expect the injury to impact Watt's availability.

Wide receiver Ben Skowronek (calf) and cornerback Brandin Echols (hamstring) were ruled out before the Steelers left for France.

item.title: Giants DC Dennard Wilson: I wasn't happy with our effort last weekend
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Giants almost pulled off a stunning comeback after putting quarterback J.J.
item.content:encoded:
The Giants almost pulled off a stunning comeback after putting quarterback J.J. McCarthy in their game against the Saints in the fourth quarter last Sunday, which is a big reason why he'll be starting against the Texans this weekend.

While the offensive coaches prepare McCarthy for his first start as a Giant, defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson is focusing on making sure the team doesn't find itself playing from behind. Next Gen Stats credited the Giants with 18 missed tackles against the Saints and Wilson said at a Thursday press conference that he doesn't believe it was "characteristic" of the team's defense.

Wilson said he specifically "wasn't happy with our effort running to the ball" and explained how he dealt with it this week.

"You confront it. Just like we do, we confront everything," Wilson said, via a transcript from the team. "When you're in the meeting room, you show those plays. I look at guys that don't run to the ball, and I call them traitors because they're traitors to the defense. At the end of the day, when you have a traitor to the defense, you either have to make adjustments to get them off the field, you have to get somebody else on the field, or they have to correct their behaviors. Last week was one of those things where we did not on every play, run to the ball, and it was unacceptable. The guys know it, and this week when you see them out there, they will be flying around 100 miles per hour with their hair on fire."

The Texans have put up 90 points over the last three weeks, so Wilson will need his words to find a willing audience if the Giants are going to avoid a third straight week without a victory.

item.title: Report: Jaguars OT Anton Harrison out for year with a torn ACL
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: When Jaguars left tackle Anton Harrison was placed on injured reserve earlier this month, word was that the results of knee surgery would determine how long he'll be out.
item.content:encoded:
When Jaguars left tackle Anton Harrison was placed on injured reserve earlier this month, word was that the results of knee surgery would determine how long he'll be out.

A report on Friday morning indicates that Harrison is going to be out for a long time. Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that surgeons discovered Harrison has a torn ACL during his procedure on Thursday.

Harrison, who was injured in Jacksonville's Week 5 win over the Eagles, will miss the rest of the season as a result of that diagnosis. Harrison will be in the final year of his rookie contract in 2027.

Walker Little took over at left tackle in Week 6 and Friday's word means that he will be set to stay there for the long term.

item.title: Steelers don't expect T.J. Watt's calf injury to affect Sunday availability
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Steelers linebacker T.J.
item.content:encoded:
Steelers linebacker T.J. Watt popped up on the team's injury report on Thursday.

Watt was listed as a limited participant in practice due to a calf injury. He was not on the report at all on Wednesday, but head coach Mike McCarthy said from Paris on Friday that he does not expect the issue to impact Watt's availability against the Saints on Sunday.

“I would say no," McCarthy said, via multiple reporters.

McCarthy added that the team's final practice on Saturday will provide a final answer to that question.

Watt has 15 tackles, 4.5 sacks, an interception return for a touchdown, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery on the season.

item.title: Mike Vrabel is proud of ex-Titan Cairo Santos, despite losing to him on Thursday night
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: In 2019, Cairo Santos was the Titans' kicker and Mike Vrabel was their head coach.
item.content:encoded:
In 2019, Cairo Santos was the Titans' kicker and Mike Vrabel was their head coach. In a Week 5 loss to the Bills, Santos missed four field goals. He was cut the next day.

That kind of outing can end a young kicker's career, but Santos kept working, signed a year later with the Bears, and has been a reliable kicker in Chicago ever since — including making the game-clinching 58-yarder in a win over Vrabel's Patriots on Thursday night.

Vrabel wasn't happy about that, but he sounded genuinely happy for Santos in his postgame comments, saying he was impressed with the way Santos shook off an earlier miss from 53 yards and said he's not sure if he had seen Santos miss a field goal since that final game as a Titan.

"Make a 58-yard field goal, I think the last field goal Cairo missed was when he kicked for the Titans," Vrabel said after the game. "I don't think he's missed one since then — he missed one earlier in the game, but we always joke about it. I'm really proud of what he's done. I didn't want him to make it tonight, but he's a former guy that we coached."

Asked if his team got out-executed, Vrabel said it was just a case of Santos making a great kick.

"I don't know how you get out-executed when a guy makes a 58-yard field goal," Vrabel said.

It was a classy postgame comment from Vrabel, who gave credit where credit is due, even in the moments after a disappointing loss.

item.title: Mike Macdonald: Kenneth Walker is playing at the highest level in the league right now
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald knows how good a running back he'll be facing when he coaches against the Chiefs on Sunday night.
item.content:encoded:
Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald knows how good a running back he'll be facing when he coaches against the Chiefs on Sunday night.

Madonald coached Kenneth Walker in Seattle, Walker won the Super Bowl MVP at the end of last season, and then Walker left for Kansas City, where he's gaining yardage a record-breaking pace.

"Ken's playing really great football," Macdonald said on SiriusXM NFL Radio. "I think it's a combination of, you see the stats and you're like, man, that's a lot of stats. And then you turn the tape on and see how they're playing and how he's playing and you're like, 'That makes sense. No one has tackled this guy yet.' It's the things we knew about Ken, that he does really well. He's so strong, he's decisive, he's got great vision. He's also come alive in the pass game. They're doing a great job with him. He's playing probably at the highest level in the league right now."

Macdonald said his defense had a big challenge on Sunday night.

"It's got to be a team effort on defense," Macdonald said. "It's gonna take waves of Seattle defense to eliminate those explosive plays he's been able to create."

item.title: Ben Johnson originally called a punt, but Cairo Santos asked to try a 58-yard field goal
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: After Bears head coach Ben Johnson initially called for a punt late in Thursday night's win over the Patriots, Bears kicker Cairo Santos convinced his coaches to let him try the 58-yard field goal that sealed the win.
item.content:encoded:
After Bears head coach Ben Johnson initially called for a punt late in Thursday night's win over the Patriots, Bears kicker Cairo Santos convinced his coaches to let him try the 58-yard field goal that sealed the win.

Earlier in the fourth quarter, Santos had missed a 53-yard field goal attempt, and Santos had never made a field goal as long as 58 yards in his NFL career. So it's easy to understand why Johnson was planning to punt. But Santos told special teams coordinator Richard Hightower, whom the players call HT, that he would make the 58-yarder if given the chance.

"I was right next to HT and Ben originally called a punt, and then the injury allowed us to talk about it. I was talking to HT that I felt good about it," Santos said. "Ben asked, 'Does he want it?' And I heard it and I told HT I want it and he said, 'Ben, Cairo says he wants it.' Thankful that Ben trusted me on that, and I delivered a great kick right down the middle."

Why was Santos confident he could make a 58-yarder only minutes after missing a 53-yarder?

"It's just who I am, really," Santos said. "The misses annoy me, but I can clear it so quick. The next opportunity, I can just lock into my routine and trust that I can execute."

Johnson was wise to trust his kicker, and that 58-yarder proved to be the play that clinched the win for the Bears.

item.title: NFL tells teams that uncalled hip-drop tackle on Aaron Rodgers was clear example of penalty
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: In Week 4, Browns defensive lineman Adin Huntington committed a textbook example of a hip-drop tackle on Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers.
item.content:encoded:
In Week 4, Browns defensive lineman Adin Huntington committed a textbook example of a hip-drop tackle on Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers. It was such a perfect example of what the hip-drop tackle rule is designed to prevent that in the NFL’s officiating video that is sent to every team, it was shown to demonstrate what not to do. Unfortunately, the officials on the field missed it.

NFL officiating and rules analyst Walt Anderson narrated Hutington's tackle on Rodgers and pointed out that it constitutes exactly what is not permitted under the hip-drop tackle rule.

"This is an illegal hip-drop tackle," Anderson said. "We want players to realize, and we're working at messaging the officials, that if they see all of the elements of this — the wrap, the swivel, the unweighting and then the dropping or trapping of legs — all four elements are clearly visible on the play. Hip-drop tackle would be the correct call. Whether this is called on the field or not, this is subject to additional discipline, including a fine."

The uncalled penalty was a big one: It happened on third down, leading the Steelers to punt. If the 15-yard penalty had been called, the Steelers would have had first-and-10 in long field goal range. The Steelers ended up losing the game by three points.

Huntington was fined, but the officials should have flagged it at the time, too. If they had, the rest of the game might have been different.

item.title: Mike Vrabel's clock management included an intentional offside penalty
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Vrabel has a long history of having his players commit penalties intentionally to manage the clock to his team's advantage.
item.content:encoded:
With 1:56 remaining in the fourth quarter on Thursday night, the Bears faced third-and-inches, and Patriots defensive lineman Cory Durden jumped offside. The fans in Chicago cheered, thinking New England had just made a big mistake. Actually, Patriots coach Mike Vrabel had just called a smart play.

Vrabel told Durden to jump offside intentionally because he figured the Patriots were unlikely to stop the Bears from picking up a first down when they only had inches to go anyway, and he'd rather concede the first down without running any time off the clock and then use his timeouts on the next set of downs.

It proved to be smart: The Patriots' defense stopped the Bears on the next three plays, the Patriots used their three timeouts, and the Bears kicked with 1:39 remaining. Unfortunately for the Patriots, Bears kicker Cairo Santos kicked a career-long 58-yard field goal that put the game effectively out of reach. But if Santos had missed, the Patriots would have had a real chance at a game-winning touchdown, and they would have had an additional 40 seconds to do it because of Vrabel's smart clock management.

Vrabel confirmed after the game what he had done, not wanting Durden to get blamed for the penalty.

"For the record, we told Cory to jump offsides on third-and-six inches," Vrabel said. "We felt like that was going to be the best way to get them stopped, and that's on me, so our guys executed. And Cairo made a huge kick."

Kirk Herbstreit, the commentator on the Prime Video broadcast of the game, correctly noted that, for the Patriots, it was better to give the Bears first-and-10 than third-and-inches in that situation.

"The fact that it's third-and-inches instead of first-and-10, actually with the clock, hurts New England," Herbstreit said after Bears quarterback Caleb Williams had been spotted just short of the first down on the previous play.

When Durden jumped offside, some thought it was a bonehead penalty, but Herbstreit knew what was happening.

"This guy did this on purpose," Herbstreit said. "Going back to the clock, we just said, if they get the first down you have to waste a timeout on the third-down conversion. Now they get the first down. Vrabel, the way he operates, that's something they would do."

Vrabel has made similar calls before. In fact, during the 2020 offseason, the NFL changed its rules to stop the clock after offensive penalties late in the fourth quarter because of the way Vrabel, then the coach of the Titans, had run the clock by intentionally committing penalties in a playoff win over the Patriots.

On Thursday night, Bears coach Ben Johnson should have declined the Patriots' offside penalty to keep it third-and-inches. But Johnson apparently hadn't thought through the consequences of accepting the penalty and the first down that came with it.

In the end, the Bears won despite Vrabel's tactic. But it was another example of how Vrabel is among the best coaches in the league at managing the clock late in the game.

item.title: Ben Johnson: Cole Kmet's knee injury doesn't look good
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Caleb Williams said after the game, "I don't have the words to describe what Cole is to me, to this team, to this organization."
item.content:encoded:
Bears tight end Cole Kmet appears to have suffered a very serious injury during Thursday night's win over the Patriots.

Coach Ben Johnson said after the game that nothing will be definitively diagnosed until Friday, but the early indications were that it's a bad injury.

“We’ll know more about it tomorrow, but I don’t think it looked very good," Johnson said.

Bears quarterback Caleb Williams said it hurt to see a player who means so much to him carted off the field.

"It was tough. I don't know exactly what it is, but getting carted off is never good. You're at least going to miss some time. I don't have the words to describe what Cole is to me, to this team, to this organization. He's the longest-tenured Bear, I believe," Williams said. "He's been through it and it's challenging. It's tough. I'll be right there with him through every step of whatever the injury is. Cole's been there for me every step of the way, through the first year, through the second year, and now through this year. I could only do the same for him."

item.title: Faulk discloses Parkinson's disease diagnosis
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Hall of Fame running back and Southern University coach Marshall Faulk has disclosed that he has Parkinson's disease.
item.content:encoded:
Hall of Fame running back and Southern University coach Marshall Faulk has disclosed that he has Parkinson's disease.

Via Jack Baer of Yahoo Sports, Faulk revealed the diagnosis in an appearance on the Caring Neurologist podcast.

"I get a physical twice a year," Faulk said. "I'm a little anal about my health. I literally asked my doctor because I noticed it as I was playing golf. I noticed the rigidity in my hand after I play a lot or practice a lot, I thought it was just normal nerves when putting and stuff like that. But it started to be times where I wasn't playing — I mean, where I was playing, but I wasn't in a match, and it would still do that.

"I was like, 'Wow, is that something? Is that normal?' And the doctor was like, 'You need to go get checked. You need to go have X, Y and Z done.'"

Faulk, a former NFL MVP, two-time NFL Offensive Player of the Year, three-time first-team All-Pro, and seven-time Pro Bowler, has been receiving treatment and taking medication.

"Since I've started on the medication, I don't really have a lot of issues," Faulk said. "I might sleep a little more. . . . Other than that, the rigidity in my hands, I still have that. Can't say that it's gotten worse. The little tremors that I get, they are what they are. I just pay attention to my gait, how I walk, when I'm working out, my ability to balance. It's still where it is.

"I don't look at it as something that's terminal. It's like, 'Hey, you get to live with this.' There's far worse things out there."

There's a known link between Parkinson's disease and football. It's one of the specific conditions that make a player who retired prior to the final settlement of the concussion class action automatically eligible for payment.

item.title: Bears TE Kmet carted off with a knee injury
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Bears quickly ruled him out.
item.content:encoded:
Bears tight end Cole Kmet injured his right knee on fourth quarter reception.

Kmet caught an 8-yard pass from Caleb Williams before linebacker Robert Spillane and cornerback Christian Gonzalez both tackled Kmet low. Kmet immediately grabbed his right knee.

Kmet couldn't put weight on his right leg and required a cart to leave the field with 5:34 remaining in the fourth quarter.

He gave a thumb's up to the Soldier Field crowd as he departed for the training room.

The Bears have ruled him out.

Kmet caught three passes for 28 yards.

item.title: Brian Schottenheimer: George Pickens "needs to understand he impacts us in the run game"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Cowboys receiver George Pickens was rewarded for a stellar contract year by being kept from getting a fair market deal.
item.content:encoded:
Cowboys receiver George Pickens was rewarded for a stellar contract year by being kept from getting a fair market deal. This year, he's playing under the franchise tag — with a second tag looming if he has another great season.

Although his per-game targets and catches through six 2026 games are roughly comparable to his 17-game average in 2025 (8.66 targets and 5.5 catches in 2026 versus 8.05 and 5.47 in 2025), his yards per game are down (71.3 yards per game in 2026 and 84.0 in 2025). He has only one 100-yard game and only one touchdown this year. (In 2025, he had five 100-yard games and nine touchdowns.)

Meanwhile, questions have emerged about Pickens's effort, especially when the ball isn't coming his way. Coach Brian Schottenheimer addressed that issue in a Thursday session with the media.

“I think GP is one of those guys where I don't ever see him really affected in terms of the emotion of, ‘Does he get the ball? Does he not get the ball?’” Schottenheimer said regarding Pickens, via Todd Archer of ESPN. “These guys play a lot of snaps. I think part of it is us rotating those guys through, but he needs to understand that he impacts us in the running game as well. And he's got to do the same thing in the run game, picking up safeties and blocking corners just like Javonte [Williams] does, picking up blitzes so he can catch balls. And that's part of the team-first mindset and GP does understand that. And when he's going, they're going to place off to his side. When he's not going, then the safeties get pretty good runs at our backs and that’s got to improve.”

Schottenheimer has been instrumental in getting the most out of Pickens during his time in Dallas. And it's a calculated risk to call him out publicly.

That said, messages like this are often sent through the media when efforts to address the situation privately haven't worked.

Regardless, Pickens (like other great receivers) wants the ball. In July, Tom Brady explained the unique mindset of the receiver position, where the players are on an island and isolated from the action unless they're getting the ball.

If the Cowboys are going to have both Pickens and CeeDee Lamb, they need to find a way to involve both of them, early and often. Like other great receivers of the past, failing to find a way to get the ball in their hands eventually will have an impact on their overall attitude.

item.title: Report: Multiple teams have trade interest in Jonathan Taylor
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: It is unclear whether the Colts will be sellers at the trade deadline.
item.content:encoded:
Multiple teams have trade interest in Colts running back Jonathan Taylor, Stephen Holder of ESPN reports. It is unclear whether the Colts will be sellers at the trade deadline.

The Colts fired General Manager Chris Ballard on Monday, with Ed Dodds serving as the interim G.M. Head coach Shane Steichen could be on his way out, too, if the 2-4 Colts can't turn it around.

Taylor, 27, led the league in carries (323), touchdowns (18) and first downs (84) last season.

"I haven't given any thought," Taylor said when asked about his future Thursday. "That'd be crazy right now, especially because we've got a great Minnesota Vikings team that we have to go against. I think it would be a discredit and a disservice to my teammates and this whole organization to think about what could, what should, what may be."

A second-round pick of the Colts in 2020, Taylor has signed two contract extensions. The most recent, a three-year deal, was signed in August and his annual average of $22 million ranks third at his position.

Taylor has 122 carries for 492 yards and seven touchdowns in six games this season. He has 1,673 carries for 8,090 yards and 76 touchdowns.

item.title: Thursday Night Football: Bears fend off Patriots 30-24
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Caleb Williams was 22-of-33 for 308 yards and two touchdowns.
item.content:encoded:
The Bears honored Mike Ditka pregame. They honored him with a win, too.

Chicago led from start to finish — though it made things interesting all night — and held off the Patriots 30-24. The Bears are 5-2 and the Patriots 4-3.

Bears kicker Cairo Santos made a career-long 58-yard field goal with 1:34 remaining to give Chicago a two-score lead. It came one snap after Caleb Williams inexplicably took a 10-yard sack on third-and-5 at the New England 30. It appeared to push the Bears out of field-goal range, but Ben Johnson trusted his kicker, who missed earlier from 53 off the right upright.

The Patriots quickly got in field-goal range, and Andy Borregales kicked a 47-yard field goal with 37 seconds remaining. Trailing by six, the Patriots tried an onside kick, but Rome Odunze recovered for the Bears.

The Bears led 10-0 early and 20-7 with 14 seconds left in the first half but allowed a last-play touchdown to the Patriots as Rhamondre Stevenson scored on a 48-yard catch-and-run. It was back and forth until time ran out on the Patriots.

Chicago outgained New England 405 to 380 as Williams went 22-of-33 for 308 yards and two touchdowns. Luther Burden caught four passes for 130 yards and a touchdown, all in the first half, and four other receivers had at least three catches.

D'Andre Swift had 22 carries for 78 yards and a touchdown.

Drake Maye was 24-of-31 for 321 yards with two touchdowns and an interception. He also ran for 26 yards and a touchdown on four carries. Stevenson had five catches for 93 yards and a touchdown and ran for 22 yards on six carries.

A.J. Brown, after his three-drop game on Sunday, had three receptions for 48 yards.

item.title: Marlon Humphrey complains about "slander" of Lamar Jackson
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey isn't happy with the manner in which Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson is treated.
item.content:encoded:
Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey isn't happy with the manner in which Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson is treated. And Humphrey said so on Thursday.

"It seems like Lamar's the only quarterback [who] kind of gets the slander that he gets for anytime anything is going on," Humphrey told reporters, via Jamison Hensley of ESPN. "I feel like you just don't see these same articles. I'm in the hot tub and it's this, that, and the third. Unfair treatment."

Humphrey didn't specify any recent examples during Jackson's absence due to an ankle injury.

"I just feel like sometimes it seems like it gets away from . . . I don't know if it's because of lack of agent or what, that no one can kind of defend him," Humphrey said. "But I do know this, if Lamar Jackson can play, if he's healthy enough to play, he will play, and that's kind of all I can say for that."

It is one of the practical consequences of not having an agent who can contact reporters, broadcasters, or anyone else in the media who is saying anything negative about Jackson. During the weeks preceding the 2018 draft, for example, there was no one to push back on the likes of former G.M. Bill Polian, who was arguing that Jackson should switch to a different position. With no established agent to defend him and advocate for him, it's possibly one of the reasons the two-time MVP was available at the bottom of round one, where he was selected 22 spots after Josh Rosen.

Ultimately, Lamar Jackson is the only one who speaks on his behalf. And Lamar doesn't seem to ever be bothered by any noise that may emerge.

Humphrey may have realized after saying what he said that Jackson may not be thrilled that Humphrey said anything.

"I think anything relating to Lamar is the thing that I don't talk about," Humphrey said. "I think the only one that really does talk about [Lamar] is Lamar. I think if Lamar can play, it'd be great. If he doesn't, we got Snoop [Huntley]."

While there have been questions in past years regarding whether Jackson chose not to play while less than 100 percent at a time when he lacked the financial security of a new contract (which is smart), there hasn't been much if any criticism of Jackson during his latest absence. He obviously has an ankle injury and, although some reports described him as day-to-day, we reported on the day it happened that he's week-to-week.

Based on his participation in practice over the past two days, this could be the week Jackson returns. And Baltimore could use him; the 4-2 Ravens host the 3-2 Bengals on Sunday.

item.title: Thursday Night Football: Luther Burden, Bears lead Patriots 20-14 at halftime
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Bears wide receiver has four catches for 130 yards and a touchdown.
item.content:encoded:
Luther Burden has 130 receiving yards, setting up three of the Bears' scoring drives with big catches.

His 26-yard reception to the New England 28 set up Cairo Santos’ 43-yard field goal. He nearly scored a 62-yard touchdown two drives later, but Kevin Byard tackled him at the New England 4 to set up D'Andre Swift’s touchdown run. His 22-yard reception set up his own 24-yard touchdown catch on a wide receiver screen with 14 seconds left in the half.

And the Bears lead the Patriots 20-14 at intermission.

It should be worse.

The Patriots got the ball back with 9 seconds left in the half and Drake Maye hit A.J. Brown for 18 yards for the wide receiver's first catch tonight. They called timeout with 3 seconds left, and with the Bears blitzing, Maye dumped the ball off to running back Rhamondre Stevenson, who ran 48 yards to the end zone.

The Bears had outgained the Patriots 211 to 161 before Stevenson's 48-yard catch-and-run.

Caleb Williams has completed 9 of 16 passes for 167 yards and a touchdown. Swift has nine carries for 37 yards and a touchdown.

The Patriots couldn't get out of their own way most of the game.

New England had a first down at the Chicago 15 with 3:32 left in the half when Maye tried to hit tight end Eli Raridon in the end zone. Instead, Bears linebacker D'Marco Jackson stepped in front of Raridon for the interception.

The Bears then got another gift from the Patriots when rookie linebacker Gabe Jacas had an inexplicable roughing-the- passer penalty. He pushed Williams long after the 22-yard pass to Burden.

Maye ended the half 12-of-15 for 169 yards with a touchdown and an interception. He also ran for 22 yards and a touchdown on three carries. Stevenson has four catches for 80 yards and a touchdown.

item.title: Tonight is Mike Vrabel's first career game at Soldier Field
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Mike Vrabel is in his 27th season as a player or coach in the NFL.
item.content:encoded:
Mike Vrabel is in his 27th season as a player or coach in the NFL.

Yet, tonight marks his first career regular-season game at Soldier Field.

Larry Mayer of the Bears' team website reported this stat that seems impossible.

Vrabel played for the Steelers (1997-2000), Patriots (2001-08) and Chiefs (2009-10); he was an assistant for the Texans (2014-17); and he was the head coach of the Titans (2018-23) and Patriots (2025-present).

He never played and has never coached in the NFC, which limits the number of times his teams have gone against the Bears on the road.

The only previous away game Vrabel had against the Bears was in 2002 as a player for the Patriots. The Bears, though, played their home games in Champaign, Illinois, that season while Soldier Field was being renovated.

The Patriots won 33-30.

As Ben Volin of the Boston Globe points out, Vrabel's Titans played preseason games at Soldier Field in 2019 and 2023.
